records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case mismatch: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is not, so 'Foo@blacklisted.com' bypasses the check
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` strings are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This allows case-variant emails like `Foo@blacklisted.com` to bypass the blacklist check.

records.issue_text: Silent email failure: errors swallowed with bare console.log, mutation returns success while guests may never receive invitations
records.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch { console.log(...) }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` with no error propagation or user-facing failure. This makes email delivery failures silent and can report success even if guest notification/invites were never sent.

records.issue_text: Seated bookings bypassed: raw attendees.createMany ignores seatsPerTimeSlot capacity and BookingSeat bookkeeping
records.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally adds new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without checking `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` / remaining seat capacity or updating any seat-specific bookkeeping. Since the handler explicitly includes `seatsPerTimeSlot` in the `CalendarEvent` it builds, this code path can add attendees beyond seat limits

records.issue_text: Unhandled organizer lookup: findFirstOrThrow with id: 0 when booking.userId is null throws a raw Prisma error (500) instead of a meaningful TRPC error
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (not a `TRPCError`), which would surface as an unhandled error/500 rather than a meaningful TRPC error. The diff shows no guarding or try/catch around this lookup.
